## Shared facts reach the real consumers

`frontend::formals` is private. Its state owns ordinal progress, preceding
Natural/Basis BinderKey sets and checked operations; an operation owns its exact
ordinary `Type<N>`, optional finite Meaning payload and three-bit access mask.
`advance` checks the original ordinal and paired spelling, installs Natural or
Basis keys without a checking callback, and invokes the profile callback only
for an Op. `into_operations` checks the complete original count and moves its
map. Neither consumer reconstructs a checked formal or derives a second
declaration mask after that move.

Finite `Compiler::abstract_bindings` still runs `signature` first. Each actual
source Op is associated through its original Forest binder; the StaticOperation
category and source span are asserted. The callback performs the same ordinary
basis classification, finite width/contract check, Meaning resolution and exact
basis-tree equality. Matrix entry cost is still charged before cloning the
finite Meaning matrix. The consumed basis, matrix and mask enter real finite
`Operation` values with the same Abstract identity string, depth 1, nodes 1 and
`abstract_value = true`. Delaying allocation of the uncharged Abstract node until
after requirements introduces no alternate checking or charge path. Checked
facts are rebuilt per declaration/call; there is no cache over mutable public
Project syntax.

Sized `declaration` consumes the checked ordinary basis into exactly one existing
Q wrapper in `Scope.operations`. Its unsupported Meaning refinement remains an
early projection rejection; the private optional payload is `Infallible` and
asserted absent. This does not promote finite Meaning or opaque Basis support
across a profile boundary.

## Association, borrowed kind checking and error priority

The sized every-function loop still locates the original declaration through
resolved DefId, module and `ast_index`. Complete static, runtime and requirement
cardinalities precede ordinal reads. Source/projected static categories, actual
Table binder keys/categories/spans and spelling are asserted at the original
ordinal. Access requirements retain their actual UseSiteId/local target; their
kind and paired metadata are checked against the original requirement. Predicate
comparisons/spans are paired. No name/span search locates a declaration, no
whole original Index is rebuilt, and no zip truncation accepts a prefix. These
are checks of private projection invariants, not semantic evidence from names.

All static-name uniqueness and all-Nat variable insertion remain before natural
premises and feasibility. Ordered kinds then borrow the actual maps/context and
the shared preceding sets. An earlier kind cannot read a later Nat, even though
the full declaration premise Context is already available. Basis placeholders
are inserted once after the corresponding shared Basis advance. The removed
kind-only Scope clone no longer copies owner/moved/operation maps or identity
counters; no prefix value map or whole Context is reconstructed.

The entire Parameter availability/substitution-capacity scan in `ty_with_prefix`
still precedes any Natural normalization. Only after that scan does unchanged
`Type::map_parts` preserve constructors, owner boundaries and left-to-right tuple
order. The recursive Natural normalizer gates actual local BinderKeys at the
existing named lookup and threads the same borrowed allowed set through Add,
Sub and Mul. It preserves each `at()` frame, left/right evaluation order,
overflow handling, nonnegative-subtraction proof and nonlinear rejection.
Unrestricted callers retain the old `natural`/`ty` wrappers with no prefix gate.
There is no eager Natural occurrence precheck or fallback by spelling.

Finite profile/resolution/dependency/signature priorities remain in their
unchanged caller. Sized still performs complete per-module projection before
declaration checks, then premises, ordered kinds, access, each runtime
name/type/bind, result and complete body/effect checks. The actual keyword span
for sized access errors and target-name span for finite errors are preserved.

## Access, providers and bounded complete checking

One common mapping defines Apply/Adjoint/Controlled as slots 0/1/2. A formal
starts with all slots false; `grant` finds only the actual local key in this
declaration's checked operation map, and rejects an unknown/wrong-kind target
or the first duplicate slot. It never consults a global or compatibility
static candidate. The unchanged finite body helper still has its previous
compatibility-candidate lookup and runtime-shadow guard; this refactor does not
claim to remove that separately retained diagnostic mechanism.

Finite body/callee checks and sized Apply, Adjoint, Controlled and forwarded
requirements consume the actual mask. Existing finite providers and both sized
provider constructors retain all three true bits only through their unchanged
implementation/type/effect checks. Meaning or an annotation grants no access;
the private representation change supplies no external provider evidence.

The finite project-wide profile, lexical indexing, dependency ordering and
every-declaration generic/concrete checking loops are unchanged. Sized still
checks every supplied private/unused function, both complete static arms and
the fold body even when the range is empty, followed by its existing effect
inference and provider obligations. Owner bind/move/drop rules are unchanged.
Finite's unsupported static-fold/profile barriers remain explicit barriers.

The diff preserves source/loading capacities, type cells/depth and substituted
Basis accounting, finite signature/basis work charges and matrix-copy order,
recursive linear implication limits, and concrete provider/evidence charges.
The sized source/storage checks still precede recursive allocation/normalization
at their existing boundaries (4096 nodes and depth 64); no new large or maximum
case was generated or checked. These are implementation capacities, not program
resource guarantees.
